title: Replica set: primary, secondaries, elections and read preference

videos.script: Lesson one promised you a database that refuses writes on purpose. This is where it happens. {{set}} A replica set is one database kept in three copies. One copy, the primary, takes every write. The other two copy it, in order, from a log. {{oplog}} Three is the smallest number that works, because two of three is a majority. And a majority decides everything here. {{majority}} It decides when a write counts as written. You will freeze two copies and watch a write wait, then fail, and still be there. {{concern}} It decides who is primary. You will stop the primary and see a new one in milliseconds. Then you will kill one, and wait nine seconds with no primary at all. {{election}} You will read from a copy that is behind, and get an old price with no warning. {{stale}} And then you will cut the primary off the network. It keeps believing it is in charge for a few seconds. It takes one order. Then it notices it is alone, and steps down. {{cut}} When the cable comes back, that order is gone, saved to a file nobody reads. By the end you will know which setting would have kept it. {{rollback}}
